title: Rex Fleet Academy: The Core Worlds
format: Prestige sequential-art educational drama; topic-based Academy lectures told as dramatic stories.
premise: Young Fleet cadets learn that the Core is not a single capital, culture, or point on a map. Each lecture uses a concrete civic, logistical, historical, or institutional problem to show how continuity after the Shattering became a civilization of interdependent worlds, stations, Crowns, markets, archives, and routes.
storyEngine: Instructor poses a practical question; cadets commit to an answer; field evidence or a historical case complicates it; the students must make a consequential decision rather than merely repeat doctrine; the lecture closes with a revised understanding that creates the next question.
canonPrinciples: The Core Worlds are Crown convergence: wealth, memory, administration, logistics, and surviving institutional continuity.
Meridian is the Core trade hub and cultural capital, but it is not a template for every Core community.
Bastion Spire is simultaneously fortress, forum, shipyard, market, memorial, and ceremonial Fleet heart.
Core institutions genuinely preserve lives and continuity; the series should not reduce the Core to a secret villain or sterile utopia.
The Core's recurring blind spot is mistaking successful continuity and central infrastructure for universal perspective or automatic legitimacy.
Fleet blue, gold, and white signify stewardship and authority; green belongs to verified safe corridors and to Verge dependence on those routes, not to Fleet identity.
Academy teaching must remain dramatic. Students question, choose, disagree, revise, and live with consequences; lectures are never wiki entries delivered by characters.

recurringFrame.primaryLocation: Rex Fleet Academy systems and civic studies wing at Bastion Spire Anchorage.
recurringFrame.tone: Intelligent, curious, occasionally argumentative. Institutional confidence is tested by concrete evidence rather than mocked.

lecturePlan.title: Meridian Is Not the Core
lecturePlan.focus: Maps, centrality, supply dependence, and the difference between a capital and a civilization.

lecturePlan.title: Who Gets a Corridor?
lecturePlan.focus: Corridor allocation under scarcity; logistics as political consequence.

lecturePlan.title: Bastion Spire
lecturePlan.focus: How fortress, market, memorial, shipyard, and civic ritual coexist in one institution.

lecturePlan.title: Children of the Schedule
lecturePlan.focus: Generational memory: people raised after stable corridors versus those formed by interruption and rationing.

lecturePlan.title: The Last Complete Census
lecturePlan.focus: Archive bias, missing populations, and the geography of records after the Shattering.

lecturePlan.title: The Cost of Resolve
lecturePlan.focus: Emergency institutions that preserve communities, and what happens when successful temporary systems become permanent.

firstLectureArc: Lysa begins by treating Meridian's prominence as proof that it is the center of the Core. A field assignment through Bastion Spire, the Anchor Markets, Meridian, and Core Spire logistics shows the cohort that different networks produce different centers. A real corridor hold forces them to confront invisible maintenance infrastructure, and the final exercise requires them to spend the Core's own privilege to protect people away from the prestigious center.
firstIssue: Issue 1 — Meridian Is Not the Core
